quests.instruction: You are heading outside to play for the afternoon. What is a good habit before you go?
quests.correctAnswer: Switch off the light as you leave 💡
options: Switch off the light as you leave 💡
Leave it on in case you come back 🔙
Turn on a second light as well 🔆
quests.hint: An empty room cannot use the light.
quests.explanation: A light left on in an empty room wastes electricity. Switching it off costs nothing and saves power.
quests.funFact: Lighting uses a noticeable share of the electricity in most homes.

quests.instruction: In which of these is a light most likely being wasted?
quests.correctAnswer: An empty hallway at noon, light on 🏠
options: An empty hallway at noon, light on 🏠
A bedroom where someone is reading 📖
A kitchen where dinner is being made 🍳
quests.hint: Ask who is using the light, and whether it is needed.
quests.explanation: No one is using the hallway and it is bright daytime, so the light is wasted. The other two are in use.
quests.funFact: Motion-sensor lights switch themselves off when nobody is in the room.

quests.instruction: Switching lights off in an empty room saves what?
quests.hint: Consider what powers a light.
quests.explanation: Lights run on electricity, which the family pays for and which has to be made. Turning them off saves both.
quests.funFact: Turning off one bulb for an hour saves only a tiny amount, but small savings add up across a whole home.

quests.instruction: What is the best thing to do with the tap while you brush your teeth?
options: Leave it running the whole time 💧
quests.hint: You only need the water at the start and the end.
quests.explanation: Water is only needed to wet the brush and to rinse. Turning the tap off in between saves many liters.
quests.funFact: A tap left running can use several liters of water a minute.

quests.instruction: You have filled your cup from the tap. What is the next step?
options: Leave it flowing a little longer 💧
quests.hint: A job is not finished until the tap is closed.
quests.explanation: Once your cup is full, the tap should be turned off firmly so it does not drip. Half off still leaks.
quests.funFact: Taps close by squeezing a rubber washer against a seat, and they wear out over time.

quests.instruction: A tap is running in an empty bathroom. What should you do first?
quests.hint: Stopping the flow is quick and easy.
quests.explanation: Turning the tap off stops the waste right away. Then you can tell a grown-up if it was left on by mistake.
quests.funFact: A tap running for ten minutes can waste enough water for several people to drink for a day.

quests.instruction: Which of these wastes the most water?
quests.correctAnswer: A hose running while no one uses it 🚿
options: A hose running while no one uses it 🚿
quests.hint: Look for water that is flowing with no one using it.
quests.explanation: A running hose delivers a lot of water every minute, and none of it is being used. Cups and hand-washing use a little, and for a reason.
quests.funFact: A garden hose can use more water in ten minutes than a whole family drinks in a day.

quests.instruction: A bucket sits under an outdoor tap that drips. What is it for?
quests.hint: A drip can be useful if you catch it.
quests.explanation: A bucket catches the dripping water, so it can be used on plants. It is better than letting the water run away.
quests.funFact: Rainwater collected in a barrel is another way to water plants without using tap water.

quests.instruction: What is a water-saving way to wash a dirty bicycle?
quests.correctAnswer: Use a bucket and a soft sponge 🪣
options: Use a bucket and a soft sponge 🪣
Leave a hose running over it 🚿
Pour a whole bath of water over it 🛁
quests.hint: Choose the way that uses only the water you need.
quests.explanation: A bucket and sponge use just enough water for the job. A running hose uses far more.
quests.funFact: A bucket of soapy water can wash a whole bicycle.

quests.instruction: Which of these needs electricity to work?
quests.hint: Look for something with a plug.
quests.explanation: A refrigerator runs on electricity to keep cold. A spoon and a dustpan work by hand.
quests.funFact: A refrigerator is one of the few appliances that runs all day and night.

quests.instruction: A phone charger stays plugged into the wall with nothing connected. What is true?
quests.correctAnswer: It may still use a little power 🔌
options: It uses as much as a fridge 🧊
It may still use a little power 🔌
quests.hint: Plugged in and idle is not always the same as off.
quests.explanation: Many chargers use a small amount of power even with nothing attached. Unplugging them when not needed saves a little.
quests.funFact: Power used by plugged-in devices that are not working is sometimes called standby power.

quests.instruction: Which habit helps save electricity at home?
quests.correctAnswer: Unplug chargers you are not using 🔌
options: Keep the TV on for background noise 📺
Unplug chargers you are not using 🔌
Open the fridge door to peek inside 🧊
quests.hint: Choose the action that stops power being used for nothing.
quests.explanation: Unplugging unused chargers stops small amounts of power being wasted. A TV left on and an open fridge both waste more.
quests.funFact: A power strip with a switch lets you turn off several devices at once.

quests.instruction: How can you use less water in the shower?
quests.hint: Water use grows with every minute.
quests.explanation: Every minute of a shower uses water, so a shorter one uses less. Turning the flow up or showering twice uses more.
quests.funFact: A shower timer or a short song helps people keep time.

quests.instruction: While you soap up in the shower, what can you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Turn the water off, then rinse 🧼
options: Turn the water off, then rinse 🧼
Let the water run onto the floor 💧
quests.hint: Soaping does not need water, and rinsing does.
quests.explanation: Turning the water off while you lather saves water and energy for heating. You turn it back on to rinse.
quests.funFact: Heating water takes a lot of energy, so saving hot water saves power too.

quests.instruction: Which of these usually uses less water?
options: A bath filled to the top 🛁
quests.hint: Consider how much water a full tub holds.
quests.explanation: A short shower often uses less water than a full tub, though a very long shower can use more. Time matters.
quests.funFact: A full bathtub can hold well over a hundred liters of water.

quests.instruction: A sheet of paper has been drawn on one side only. What can you do with it?
quests.hint: Look at which part of the page has not been used.
quests.explanation: Using the blank side is reuse: it gives the paper a second life before it is recycled. That saves paper.
quests.funFact: Scrap paper is great for notes, lists, and rough drawings.

quests.instruction: Which of these is reusing, and not recycling?
quests.correctAnswer: Turning a box into a toy garage 📦
options: Putting a bottle in the recycling bin ♻️
Turning a box into a toy garage 📦
Throwing a can in the trash 🗑️
quests.hint: Reusing keeps the same item for a new purpose.
quests.explanation: Reusing means using an object again, in the same form, for a new job. Recycling breaks things down to make new items.
quests.funFact: Reuse is often better than recycling, since it needs no energy to remake the item.

quests.instruction: Why is reusing something often better than throwing it away?
quests.hint: Think about what it takes to make a new thing.
quests.explanation: Making new things uses materials, water, and energy. Reusing what we already have avoids all of that.
quests.funFact: Many towns have sharing groups or markets for things that are still useful.

quests.instruction: On a bright morning, how can you get light in a room without using electricity?
quests.hint: The sun is already shining.
quests.explanation: Daylight through a window is free and does not use electricity. Candles are a fire risk and are for grown-ups.
quests.funFact: Sunlight can reach quite far into a room when walls are painted a light color.

quests.instruction: Where is a good spot to read during the day, without turning on a lamp?
options: In the darkest corner of the room 🌑
quests.hint: Natural light is strongest right beside the glass.
quests.explanation: Near a window, there is plenty of light for reading without a lamp. A dark corner would strain your eyes.
quests.funFact: Reading in good light is easier on your eyes than reading in dim light.

quests.instruction: When is a lamp really needed?
quests.correctAnswer: When it is dark or hard to see 🌙
options: All day, even when it is sunny ☀️
When it is dark or hard to see 🌙
quests.hint: Light helps you see, so use it when you cannot.
quests.explanation: A lamp is useful when there is not enough natural light to see well. In bright daytime or when nobody is using the room, it is not needed.
quests.funFact: A task lamp lights only the area you need, rather than the whole room.

quests.instruction: A tap keeps dripping even after it is turned off. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a grown-up it needs fixing 🔧
options: Tell a grown-up it needs fixing 🔧
quests.hint: A repair job needs the right person and the right tools.
quests.explanation: A dripping tap needs a new washer or part, which a grown-up can arrange. Taking taps apart could cause a leak.
quests.funFact: A tap that drips once a second can waste thousands of liters in a year.

quests.instruction: Why does a small drip matter?
quests.correctAnswer: It adds up to a lot of water 💧
options: It adds up to a lot of water 💧
quests.hint: Work out what happens with a drip every second, all day.
quests.explanation: A drip may seem tiny, but dozens each minute, every day, all year, add up to many bathtubs of water.
quests.funFact: Fixing a dripping tap is usually a quick and cheap repair.

quests.instruction: The toilet keeps running water after you flush. What should you do?
quests.hint: Some problems need an adult who knows how to fix them.
quests.explanation: A toilet that keeps running wastes a lot of water, so a grown-up should know. Flushing again or poking inside will not fix it.
quests.funFact: A running toilet can waste many liters of water every hour.

quests.instruction: Which way of washing a few plates uses the least water?
quests.correctAnswer: Use a basin of soapy water 🍽️
options: Use a basin of soapy water 🍽️
Rinse each under a running tap 🚰
Fill a sink for each plate 🛁
quests.hint: Think about water poured away, not used.
quests.explanation: A basin of soapy water cleans many plates using one fill. Running water over each plate wastes a lot.
quests.funFact: A quick rinse in a second basin can replace a running tap.

quests.instruction: Which saves more electricity on a chilly day?
quests.hint: Warmth can come from you, too.
quests.explanation: A sweater keeps your own warmth in, without using any electricity. Heating a whole house uses a lot.
quests.funFact: Putting on layers often lets families turn their heating down a little.

quests.instruction: Which lunch container is the best choice for the planet?
quests.hint: Consider what ends up in the trash.
quests.explanation: A washable box can be used again and again. Bags and foil are thrown away after one use.
quests.funFact: A good lunch box can last for many school years.

quests.instruction: A family wants to cut how much water they use. Which plan works best?
options: Run the tap while brushing teeth 🚰
Water the garden at midday heat ☀️
quests.hint: Pick the plan that wastes the least water.
quests.explanation: Fixing drips and shortening showers cut waste in two places. The other plans use more water or lose it to evaporation.
quests.funFact: Watering plants in the early morning or evening wastes less, because less water evaporates.

quests.instruction: Why does saving water matter even where water seems plentiful?
quests.correctAnswer: Cleaning and moving it takes energy 🚰
options: Taps break if used too much 🔧
Cleaning and moving it takes energy 🚰
quests.hint: Water gets to a tap through lots of work.
quests.explanation: Water has to be collected, cleaned, and pumped to homes, and that takes energy. Wasting it wastes all that effort too.
quests.funFact: Some places have plenty of rain one season and very little the next.

quests.instruction: Which action saves both electricity and water?
options: Using the dryer for a single sock 🧦
quests.hint: Look for the choice that makes each cycle count.
quests.explanation: A full load washes more clothes in one cycle than two half loads, so it saves water, electricity, and time.
quests.funFact: Many machines use almost the same amount of water and power whether they are full or not.
